scenario: Care manager confirms hospice election details with member's daughter after intake visit; member has moved in with her
text:
CM: Hi, good afternoon, this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Renata]] with Cadence care management. Am I speaking with, um, [[RELATIVE_NAME:Joanne Pruitt]]?
DAUGHTER: Yes, this is [[RELATIVE_NAME:Joanne]]. Is this about my dad?
CM: It is, it's about [[NAME:Harold]]. I saw a note that the hospice intake nurse came out to the house [[DATE:yesterday]]?
DAUGHTER: She did, she was here almost two hours. Her name was, uh, [[PROVIDER_NAME:Bev]], [[PROVIDER_NAME:Beverly]] something, from [[ORGANIZATION:Gentle Harbor Hospice]].
CM: Okay good. So for the election paperwork I just need to confirm a couple things. Can you give me his date of birth?
DAUGHTER: [[DOB:November ninth, nineteen thirty-eight]].
CM: Thank you. And his member ID, it's on the Cadence card.
DAUGHTER: Hang on, the card's in his wallet... okay it's [[MEMBER_ID:C, D, four four seven, one nine oh two]].
CM: [[MEMBER_ID:C D four four seven one nine zero two]]. Perfect.
DAUGHTER: He's eighty-seven now and honestly the COPD has just, I mean he can't get to the bathroom without the oxygen anymore. He's on four liters.
CM: I'm so sorry. That's really what hospice is for. Has [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Lindqvist]] signed the certification yet?
DAUGHTER: Doctor who? Oh, [[PROVIDER_NAME:Lindqvist]], his lung doctor. I think so, they said he faxed it [[DATE:Friday]].
CM: Okay. And the address we have is [[ADDRESS:forty-two eleven Sumner Road]], is that still where he's staying?
DAUGHTER: No, no, that's the thing, he moved in with me back in [[DATE:August]]. I'm at [[ADDRESS:nine eighteen Calloway Court]], [[CITY:Bellbrook]], [[ZIP:four five three oh five]].
CM: Got it. Is that [[ADDRESS:Calloway]] with two L's?
DAUGHTER: Two L's, yep. [[ADDRESS:C A L L O W A Y]].
CM: And the best callback number for you?
DAUGHTER: My cell, [[PHONE:nine three seven, five five five, zero one six two]].
CM: Great. The hospice team usually starts visits within forty-eight hours of the signed election. They'll probably come Mondays and Thursdays to start, and the aide can help with baths.
DAUGHTER: Okay. Thank you, [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Renata]], really. This has been a lot.
CM: Of course. Call me anytime, I'm here Monday through Friday.

scenario: Three-way call with DME supplier about insulin pump supplies on hold for an expired prescription
text:
CM: Okay, I think we're connected. Hi, this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Marcus Feld]] from Cadence, I have our member [[NAME:Priya Raman]] on the line with me.
DME: Hi, thanks for holding, this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Tonya]] in the pump department at [[ORGANIZATION:Brightline Diabetic Supply]]. Can I get the patient's date of birth?
MEMBER: It's [[DOB:four, twelve, ninety-one]].
DME: And the last name, sorry, was that [[NAME:Raman]], [[NAME:R A M A N]]?
MEMBER: Yes. First name [[NAME:Priya]], [[NAME:P R I Y A]].
DME: Okay I see her. Last order shipped... [[DATE:July twenty-second]], so she's due for infusion sets and reservoirs.
MEMBER: Right, I'm completely out of reservoirs as of, like, [[DATE:this morning]]. I've been stretching them.
CM: Is there a hold on the account? She said she got a letter.
DME: Yeah, there's a hold because we need a new prescription. The one from [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Achebe]] expired on [[DATE:the thirtieth]].
MEMBER: But I just saw her [[DATE:two weeks ago]]!
DME: She may not have sent it over. Happens a lot.
CM: I'll call [[FACILITY_NAME:Northgate Endocrine]] right after this. What's the account number so they can reference it?
DME: Account is [[ACCOUNT_ID:B L, L as in Lima, seven seven zero, four eight three]].
CM: [[ACCOUNT_ID:B L seven seven zero four eight three]].
DME: Correct. Once the prescription is in we can overnight it. Is she still at [[ADDRESS:twenty-six oh one Marigold Lane, apartment three B]]?
MEMBER: Yes, but please don't leave it on the step, the box got stolen last time. Can you make it signature required?
DME: I'll flag signature required. So that's the three hundred unit cartridges, a ten-pack, and the twenty-three inch tubing sets.
CM: And just so you have it for quantity, she runs about forty-five units a day total, basal plus boluses.
MEMBER: Can you email me the tracking? It's [[EMAIL:priya dot raman ninety-one at example dot net]].
DME: [[EMAIL:Priya dot raman nine one... at example dot net]]. Got it. I'll leave it pending prescription and you'll get an email when it ships.

scenario: Member and son call about broken power wheelchair joystick; vendor delay, rural address
text:
CM: Cadence care management, this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Ines]], how can I help?
MEMBER: Yeah hi, it's [[NAME:Walter Delacroix]], uh, [[NAME:D E L A C R O I X]], you all helped me get the power chair last year.
CM: Hi Mister [[NAME:Delacroix]]. Yes I see you. What's going on with the chair?
MEMBER: The joystick, it just quit on me [[DATE:Saturday night]]. Lights come on, won't go. I've been stuck in the recliner, my son's had to—
SON: Dad, let me, let me talk to her. Hi, this is [[RELATIVE_NAME:Andre]], his son.
CM: Hi [[RELATIVE_NAME:Andre]]. Mister [[NAME:Delacroix]], you're okay with me talking with him?
MEMBER: Yeah, yeah, go ahead.
SON: So we called the vendor, [[ORGANIZATION:Ridgeway Mobility]], and they said the earliest tech is [[DATE:a week from Thursday]]. He can't wait that long. He's got MS, he's seventy-three, he's two hundred forty pounds, I can't keep lifting him.
CM: Understood. Did they give you a work order number?
SON: Uh, [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:R W dash, one one eight, wait, one one nine four six]].
CM: [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:R W one one nine four six]]. Okay. I'm going to call their service manager and push for an expedited visit, and in the meantime I'll see about a loaner manual chair.
SON: That'd help a lot. Tell them to come to the house, it's [[ADDRESS:Rural Route four, box ninety-one]], out past the [[GEOGRAPHIC_CONTEXT:Dollar General on seventeen]], in [[CITY:Harlan]].
CM: [[ADDRESS:Rural Route four, box ninety-one]]. And the best number to reach you?
SON: Mine, [[PHONE:six oh six, five five five, zero one three eight]]. His landline's dead half the time.
CM: Got it. Just to verify for the vendor, his member ID?
MEMBER: I got it right here. [[MEMBER_ID:nine nine oh four, two two one, eight seven]].
CM: Thank you. I'll call you back within a couple hours either way.
SON: Thanks [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Ines]].

scenario: Member on dialysis received pay-or-quit notice; care manager refers to rental assistance
text:
CM: Hi, is this [[NAME:Keisha]]? It's [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Dolores]] from Cadence, returning your call.
MEMBER: Yes, hi, thank you for calling back, I'm kind of freaking out.
CM: Take your time. What happened?
MEMBER: So the landlord taped a notice on my door [[DATE:Monday]], it says I've got fourteen days or they file. I'm behind two months because I was out after the fistula surgery and [[EMPLOYER:Harmon Logistics]] never paid the short-term disability like they said they would.
CM: Okay. That's a lot to deal with. First, are you still on [[ADDRESS:Wexford Terrace]]?
MEMBER: Yeah, [[ADDRESS:fourteen ten Wexford Terrace, unit two oh seven]].
CM: [[ADDRESS:Two oh seven]], right. Does the notice have a case number or anything?
MEMBER: No, it just says notice to pay or quit. Nothing's been filed yet I don't think.
CM: Good, that gives us some room. I'm going to refer you to the emergency rental assistance program through [[ORGANIZATION:Tri-County Community Action]], and there's a free legal aid clinic, they do walk-ins on Wednesdays at the library.
MEMBER: Wednesdays I can do. Dialysis is Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday.
CM: Perfect. For the application they'll want proof of income, the notice, and your lease. Do you have an email so I can send you the form?
MEMBER: It's [[EMAIL:k underscore bellamy at example dot org]]. [[NAME:Bellamy]], [[NAME:B E L L A M Y]].
CM: Got it. And date of birth for the referral?
MEMBER: [[DOB:June third, eighty-four]].
CM: Okay, [[NAME:Miss Bellamy]], I'm sending the referral now. Also, do you want me to talk to your social worker at the unit about the disability paperwork?
MEMBER: Please. Her name's [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Ayesha]], she's there on dialysis days.
CM: I'll reach out to her. You did the right thing calling.
MEMBER: Thank you so much, [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Dolores]].

scenario: Care manager books an in-person Haitian Creole interpreter for a cardiology follow-up
text:
CM: Hi, I need to book an in-person interpreter. This is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Paul Wen]] with Cadence.
AGENCY: Sure, [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Yvette]] here at [[ORGANIZATION:Bridgeword Language Services]]. What language?
CM: [[LANGUAGE:Haitian Creole]]. It's for a member, last name [[NAME:Jean-Baptiste]], first name [[NAME:Marie-Claude]].
AGENCY: Can you spell the last name for me?
CM: [[NAME:J E A N, hyphen, B A P T I S T E]].
AGENCY: Okay. And the appointment?
CM: It's a cardiology follow-up at [[FACILITY_NAME:Lakeview Heart and Vascular]], [[ADDRESS:three thirty North Halsted, suite four hundred]]. With [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Sorensen]]. [[DATE:October twenty-third]] at nine forty-five.
AGENCY: [[DATE:Twenty-third]], nine forty-five. How long should I book?
CM: Ninety minutes, they're doing an echo too. She's seventy-nine, she's got A fib, they're adjusting her Eliquis. And, um, she prefers a female interpreter if that's possible.
AGENCY: We have [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Fabienne]] that morning, she does a lot of medical. Do you have a member ID for billing?
CM: Yes, it's [[MEMBER_ID:M C, zero zero four, five five, nine one, two, sorry, scratch that, nine one three]].
AGENCY: So [[MEMBER_ID:M C zero zero four five five nine one three]].
CM: That's it.
AGENCY: And a contact for day-of, in case she's running late?
CM: Her son [[RELATIVE_NAME:Wesner]] usually brings her. His cell is [[PHONE:seven seven three, five five five, zero one nine one]]. Please make sure the clinic doesn't just use him to interpret, she's asked for a professional.
AGENCY: Noted, I'll put that in the job notes. Your confirmation number is [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:B W, two six eight eight one]].
CM: [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:B W two six eight eight one]]. Thank you, [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Yvette]].

scenario: School nurse calls care manager about a pediatric member's asthma episodes and expired inhaler
text:
SCHOOL_NURSE: Hi, this is [[PROVIDER_NAME:Gail Herrington]], I'm the nurse over at [[FACILITY_NAME:Pinecrest Elementary]]. I'm calling about a student, [[NAME:Mateo Villanueva]], his mom signed a release for us to talk with his care manager.
CM: Yes, hi, I'm [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Hannah]], I have [[NAME:Mateo]]. What's going on?
SCHOOL_NURSE: So a couple things. The inhaler we keep here expired, and he's had three episodes in the last two weeks. [[DATE:Yesterday]] he needed the albuterol twice before lunch, two puffs each time.
CM: Oh, that's not good. Can you confirm his date of birth for me?
SCHOOL_NURSE: [[DOB:February fourteenth, twenty seventeen]]. Valentine's baby.
CM: Yep, that's him. And do you have a Medicaid number on your form?
SCHOOL_NURSE: I only have the last four, it's [[MEMBER_ID:two eight eight one]].
CM: That matches. Has mom been able to get him in to [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Mbeki]]?
SCHOOL_NURSE: That's the thing, [[RELATIVE_NAME:Lucia]], his mom, works nights at the [[EMPLOYER:Tyson plant]] and she's been having a hard time. She said the clinic only does mornings.
CM: Okay. I can help with that, there's a pediatric clinic with Saturday hours. What number do you have for her?
SCHOOL_NURSE: The one on our emergency card is [[PHONE:four seven nine, five five five, zero one zero four]].
CM: Hm, that's different from ours, ours ends in, um, [[PHONE:oh one five two]]. I'll try both.
SCHOOL_NURSE: Also, he has PE on Tuesdays and Fridays and the gym teacher wants a note about pre-treating before exercise.
CM: Makes sense. I'll ask the doctor for an updated asthma action plan and a new school inhaler. Where should I send it?
SCHOOL_NURSE: You can email me, [[EMAIL:g herrington at example dot org]], that's [[EMAIL:g, h, e, double r, i, n, g, t, o, n]].
CM: Got it. Thank you for calling, this is really helpful.

scenario: Member's niece, newly appointed guardian, sends guardianship letters so care manager can update authorized contacts
text:
CM: Hello, this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Bridget]] calling from Cadence. I'm looking for [[RELATIVE_NAME:Sunita]]?
NIECE: Speaking. Is this about my uncle?
CM: Yes, about [[NAME:Mister Kapoor]]. I got your voicemail that the guardianship went through.
NIECE: It did, finally. The judge signed the letters of guardianship on [[DATE:September eighteenth]]. It took almost five months.
CM: Congratulations, I know that's been a long road. To update his file I'll need a copy of the letters. Can you read me the case number?
NIECE: Sure, it's, um, [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:two five, G A, zero zero three one seven]], from [[ORGANIZATION:Franklin County Probate Court]].
CM: [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:Two five G A zero zero three one seven]]. And just to verify I have the right member, his date of birth?
NIECE: [[DOB:March second, nineteen forty-five]]. He's eighty-one.
CM: Thank you. And he's still at [[FACILITY_NAME:Willow Bend]]?
NIECE: Yes, [[FACILITY_NAME:Willow Bend Memory Care]], on the second floor now. They moved him after the fall [[DATE:last month]]. His resident number there is [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:W B, four four zero two]], if you need it.
CM: That's helpful. And for our records, how do you spell your full name?
NIECE: [[RELATIVE_NAME:Sunita]], [[RELATIVE_NAME:S U N I T A]], and the last name is [[RELATIVE_NAME:Kapoor-Hayes]], with a hyphen. [[RELATIVE_NAME:K A P O O R]], hyphen, [[RELATIVE_NAME:H A Y E S]].
CM: And where should I email the authorization form?
NIECE: [[EMAIL:sunita dot k h at example dot com]].
CM: Okay. Once that's signed, you'll be the decision-maker on file. I'll also let [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Petrakis]] know, since she does his memory care visits.
NIECE: Good. His Alzheimer's has gotten a lot worse, he's on the Namenda and the donepezil, and honestly I don't know if they're doing anything anymore.
CM: That's a good question for the next care conference. They do those every ninety days.
NIECE: Okay. Thank you, [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Bridget]].

scenario: Care manager coordinates a biologic prior authorization appeal with rheumatology office staff
text:
OFFICE: Rheumatology, this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Kenji]].
CM: Hi [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Kenji]], it's [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Shauna]] from Cadence care management. I'm calling about [[NAME:Gloria Esposito]], the denial on her biologic.
OFFICE: Oh yes, [[NAME:Mrs. Esposito]]. Hold on, let me pull her up. Date of birth?
CM: [[DOB:Eight, nineteen, fifty-eight]].
OFFICE: Okay. Yeah, we got the denial letter, it's dated [[DATE:September twenty-ninth]]. They're saying step therapy wasn't documented.
CM: But she was on methotrexate for, what, eighteen months? And she had the liver enzymes go up.
OFFICE: Right, and then sulfasalazine, she couldn't tolerate it. It's all in the chart, it just didn't get attached. [[PROVIDER_NAME:Doctor Abboud]] wants to do a peer-to-peer and a written appeal.
CM: Great. We have sixty days from the letter, so we're fine on time. Can you give me the reference number from the denial?
OFFICE: It's [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:P A two six, dash, seven seven three one zero]].
CM: [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:P A two six seven seven three one zero]]. And what member ID did you submit under? I want to make sure it's not the old one.
OFFICE: [[MEMBER_ID:R, X, four oh one, D as in David, eight eight five]].
CM: Was that a B or a D?
OFFICE: D as in David.
CM: Okay, that's current. And I'll need [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Abboud]]'s NPI for the appeal form.
OFFICE: [[NPI:one four eight two, six six zero, three nine one]].
CM: [[NPI:One four eight two six six zero three nine one]]. Perfect. Her CRP last time was twenty-four and she said her hands are so swollen she can't open jars.
OFFICE: Yeah, she was in tears at the last visit. We'll send the letter of medical necessity by [[DATE:Wednesday]].
CM: Thank you. Can you cc me? [[EMAIL:s dot oduya at example dot com]].
OFFICE: Got it.

scenario: Oxygen delivery driver lost on a rural route; care manager conferences in the member's wife for directions
text:
DRIVER: Yeah, hi, I'm the driver from [[ORGANIZATION:Clearbreath Home Medical]], I got a delivery for a, uh, [[NAME:Eldon Yoder]], and the GPS has me in the middle of a cornfield.
CM: Oh no. Okay, this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Trevor]] at Cadence, I'm his care manager. What address do you have?
DRIVER: [[ADDRESS:Seventeen County Road two twelve]], [[CITY:Millersburg]].
CM: That's right. Let me get his wife on the line, hold on... [[RELATIVE_NAME:Ruth]]? Hi, it's [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Trevor]] from Cadence, I've got the oxygen driver here, he can't find the house.
WIFE: Oh for heaven's sake, they always do that. Where is he?
DRIVER: I'm by a red barn, there's a hand-painted sign for brown eggs.
WIFE: Okay, you went too far. Turn around, go back about a mile, and we're the white house with the green roof, right across from the [[GEOGRAPHIC_CONTEXT:Salt Creek Mennonite church]]. Mailbox says [[NAME:Yoder]], but half the road says [[NAME:Yoder]], so look for the church.
DRIVER: Got it, church, white house, green roof.
CM: While I have you, can you confirm the order? I want to make sure it's the right setup.
DRIVER: Order number [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:C B, three three oh, seven one six]]. Five liter concentrator, twelve E tanks, a conserving regulator, and fifty feet of tubing.
WIFE: Fifty feet? He's on two liters continuous, the doctor said, and he sleeps upstairs.
CM: That's right, two liters per minute, and up to three with exertion. Fifty feet should get him from the bedroom to the bathroom.
WIFE: Well, the last company only brought twenty-five and he kept pulling it off the nightstand.
DRIVER: I'll show him how to do the tank swap too. Is he home all day?
WIFE: He's not going anywhere, honey. He's ninety-one.
CM: [[RELATIVE_NAME:Ruth]], the respiratory therapist from [[ORGANIZATION:Clearbreath]] will call to set up a visit, probably [[DATE:early next week]]. Is the house phone still the best number?
WIFE: Yes, [[PHONE:three three oh, five five five, zero one two nine]]. We don't do cell phones.
CM: Perfect. Driver, you're good?
DRIVER: Turning around now.

scenario: Cadence nurse calls member back with A1c and potassium results and arranges repeat lab
text:
RN: Hi, this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Corinne]], I'm a nurse with Cadence. May I speak with [[NAME:Tomasz Wisniewski]]?
MEMBER: That's me, but everybody calls me [[NAME:Tom]]. You got my labs?
RN: I do. Before I go over them, can you verify your date of birth and address?
MEMBER: [[DOB:January twenty-sixth, nineteen sixty]]. And it's [[ADDRESS:fifty-five Orchard Hill Drive]].
RN: Thank you, [[NAME:Tom]]. So these are from the draw at [[FACILITY_NAME:Harborview Lab]] on [[DATE:the twenty-ninth]]. Your A1c came back at nine point two.
MEMBER: Nine point two? It was eight something in the spring.
RN: It was eight point one in [[DATE:April]], yeah. So it's gone up. Have you been taking the metformin?
MEMBER: Mostly. I, um, I ran out for a week or so when the pharmacy messed up the refill.
RN: Okay, that happens. The other thing is your potassium was five point six, which is a little high, and [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Oyelaran]] wants to repeat it to make sure it wasn't a bad sample.
MEMBER: Is that dangerous?
RN: Mildly elevated. She wants it rechecked within a few days, and she said hold off on the salt substitute if you're using one, those are mostly potassium.
MEMBER: My wife bought the no-salt stuff! [[RELATIVE_NAME:Bozena]], hey, it's the potassium salt.
RN: That could definitely be part of it. Can you get to the lab [[DATE:Wednesday the eighth]]? They're open seven to three.
MEMBER: [[DATE:Wednesday]]'s fine. Do I need a new order?
RN: It's already in. Just bring your ID and give them your medical record number, it's [[MRN:H V, zero zero six, two two four, seven nine]].
MEMBER: Hold on, writing. [[MRN:H V... was it two two four seven nine]]?
RN: [[MRN:Zero zero six, then two two four, then seven nine]].
MEMBER: Got it. And can you text me a reminder? My cell is [[PHONE:two oh seven, five five five, zero one five nine]].
RN: I'll set that up. And, [[NAME:Tom]], your last name, is it [[NAME:W I S N I E W S K I]]? I want the text to have it right.
MEMBER: Perfect, most people forget the second W.

scenario: Dialysis social worker reports member missed two treatments after transport no-shows
text:
SW: Hi, this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Colleen Matsuda]], I'm the social worker at [[FACILITY_NAME:Riverside Kidney Center]]. I'm trying to reach the care manager for [[NAME:Darnell Hutchins]].
CM: That's me, [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Ravi]]. Is [[NAME:Darnell]] okay?
SW: Well, that's why I'm calling. He missed [[DATE:Tuesday]] and [[DATE:Thursday]] this week. He's normally very consistent, Tuesday Thursday Saturday, first shift.
CM: Oh, that's not like him at all. Did anybody reach him?
SW: I finally got him [[DATE:last night]]. He said his ride never came. Both days. He's with [[ORGANIZATION:MedRide]] through the plan.
CM: Ugh. Okay. Did he say anything about how he's feeling?
SW: He's short of breath, his ankles are swollen, and his weight's probably up. He was already running about three kilos over his dry weight [[DATE:last Saturday... sorry, not last Saturday, the Saturday before]]. And his potassium was borderline.
CM: Should he be going to the ER?
SW: Our nephrologist, [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Castellanos]], wants him in for an extra treatment [[DATE:today]] if we can get him here by noon. Otherwise, yes, the ER.
CM: Okay, I'll set up a direct ride, not through the broker. He's still at the corner of [[ADDRESS:Fifth and Linden]], right? The building with the laundromat?
SW: That's what we have. [[ADDRESS:Two forty Linden Avenue]], [[CITY:Elizabeth]].
CM: And you have a good number for him?
SW: His cell's been cutting out. His girlfriend [[RELATIVE_NAME:Tasha]] picked up the second time, her number is [[PHONE:nine oh eight, five five five, zero one eight seven]].
CM: [[PHONE:Nine oh eight, five five five, oh one eight seven]]. Okay. Let me get the ride booked and I'll call you right back with a pickup time.
SW: Thank you. Our chair opens at eleven thirty.

scenario: Exhausted spouse caregiver of member with Parkinson's discusses respite options
text:
CM: Hi [[RELATIVE_NAME:Linda]], it's [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Joel]] from Cadence. I'm just checking in on you and [[NAME:Frank]].
CAREGIVER: Oh. Hi. Sorry, I, I was just sitting down. It's been a day.
CM: That's okay. How are things?
CAREGIVER: Honestly? Not good. He fell again [[DATE:last Sunday]], in the bathroom, and I couldn't get him up. I had to call the fire department to come lift him. And he was up all night [[DATE:Tuesday]], the hallucinations, he thought there were kids in the yard.
CM: That sounds really exhausting. Are you getting any sleep?
CAREGIVER: Maybe four hours. And I still have my shifts at [[EMPLOYER:Giant Eagle]], three mornings a week, because we need the money. I'm, I'm seventy-two years old. I can't...
CM: Take your time.
CAREGIVER: Sorry. My sister [[RELATIVE_NAME:Margit]] keeps telling me to put him in a home, but she's in [[CITY:Cleveland]], she doesn't see it.
CM: [[RELATIVE_NAME:Linda]], what you're describing is caregiver burnout, and it's really common with Parkinson's. You don't have to choose between doing everything and a nursing home. Is he still going to [[FACILITY_NAME:Sunrise Adult Day]]?
CAREGIVER: Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, yes. That's the only time I breathe.
CM: Okay. I'd like to refer you to [[ORGANIZATION:Lake Erie Area Agency on Aging]] for in-home respite, they can send an aide for a few hours or do a short overnight stay somewhere. And there's a caregiver support group on Thursday evenings.
CAREGIVER: I don't know if I can do a group.
CM: That's fine, no pressure. Also, the hallucinations, I want to let [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Haddad]] know, sometimes the carbidopa levodopa timing or another med can cause that.
CAREGIVER: Okay. Yes. Please. Oh, and our fiftieth anniversary is [[DATE:the nineteenth]], I, I just want him to be home for that.
CM: Then let's make that the goal. I'll call you back with the respite intake info. Is this home number still best?
CAREGIVER: Yes, [[PHONE:four four zero, five five five, zero one four one]].

scenario: Care manager helps a Vietnam-era veteran member start a VA Aid and Attendance claim
text:
CM: Mister [[NAME:Whitfield]], it's [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Alana]] with Cadence. Is this a good time?
MEMBER: Good as any. Call me [[NAME:Clarence]].
CM: Okay, [[NAME:Clarence]]. Last time you mentioned you served, and I wanted to follow up about VA benefits, specifically Aid and Attendance, that could help pay for an aide.
MEMBER: Yeah. Army, sixty-nine to seventy-one. Vietnam. I never did anything with the VA though, my wife always said we didn't need it.
CM: Well, with the diabetes and the neuropathy there may be a presumptive connection, because of Agent Orange. Do you have your DD two fourteen?
MEMBER: Somewhere. My daughter [[RELATIVE_NAME:Renee]] has a box of papers, she lives out in [[STATE:Arizona]] now.
CM: That's okay, the veterans service officer can request it. I'd like to connect you with [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Ramon Escobedo]], he's at the [[ORGANIZATION:Marion County Veterans Service Office]]. They do this for free.
MEMBER: [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Ramon]]. Okay.
CM: Do you remember your service number, or did they use your social?
MEMBER: Back then it was a service number. I know this one by heart, [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:R A, five four, one one six, two zero eight]].
CM: [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:R A five four one one six two zero eight]]. I'll pass that along. Have you ever been seen at [[FACILITY_NAME:the Halstead VA clinic]]?
MEMBER: Once, maybe [[DATE:two summers ago]], for a hearing test. They gave me hearing aids I never wear.
CM: [[NAME:Clarence]]! Okay, we'll talk about that another time. [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Ramon]] will want to meet in person. He does home visits on Fridays. Would [[DATE:Friday the seventeenth]] work?
MEMBER: I don't go anywhere. Sure.
CM: And you're still on [[ADDRESS:Tecumseh Street]], the house by the [[GEOGRAPHIC_CONTEXT:old Shell station]]?
MEMBER: [[ADDRESS:Four oh nine Tecumseh]]. Tell him the doorbell don't work, knock loud.
CM: Ha, I will. He'll call you first from his office line. You're seventy-five, right? I just want to note it on the referral.
MEMBER: Seventy-six in [[DATE:December]].
CM: Got it. I'll send the referral [[DATE:today]] and call you after he reaches out.

scenario: Member and care manager call mail-order pharmacy to switch shipping to a PO box and fix a split refill
text:
PHARMACY: Thank you for calling [[FACILITY_NAME:CareDirect Mail Pharmacy]], my name is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Devon]], who am I speaking with?
MEMBER: This is [[NAME:Rosalind Tafoya]], and I've got my care manager on with me.
CM: Hi, [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Esperanza]] from Cadence.
PHARMACY: Hi both. [[NAME:Ms. Tafoya]], can I get your date of birth and zip code?
MEMBER: [[DOB:May fifth, nineteen fifty-two]], and zip is [[ZIP:eight eight oh six one]].
PHARMACY: Thank you. How can I help?
MEMBER: Well, my packages keep getting left at the road and the heat ruins them. I got a P O box now. I want everything sent there.
PHARMACY: Sure. Go ahead with the box.
MEMBER: [[ADDRESS:P O Box four eighty-eight]], [[CITY:Silver City]], [[STATE:New Mexico]], same zip.
PHARMACY: [[ADDRESS:P O Box four eight eight]]. Okay, updated. Anything else?
CM: Yes, her metoprolol. She takes twenty-five milligrams, half a tab twice a day, but the last shipment only had thirty tablets, which is a month, not ninety days.
PHARMACY: Let me look. Prescription number?
MEMBER: It's on the bottle... [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:seven oh, two two, nine, one four, six]].
PHARMACY: Hmm, I'm not finding that. Can you read it again?
MEMBER: [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:Seven oh two two nine one four... six. Oh wait, no, that's a three at the end, my glasses. Seven oh two two nine one four three]].
PHARMACY: There it is. Yeah, it was entered as thirty days. I'll need a new script from the prescriber for the ninety-day.
CM: That's [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Benally]] at [[FACILITY_NAME:Gila Family Health]]. I'll call them.
PHARMACY: Perfect. Her Eliquis and atorvastatin are scheduled to ship [[DATE:October fourteenth]], so if we get the metoprolol by then we'll bundle them.
MEMBER: And to the P O box.
PHARMACY: To the P O box, yes ma'am.

scenario: Member reports bedbug infestation and skin bites; care manager helps file complaint with housing authority
text:
MEMBER: Hello? Is this, um, Cadence? I need to talk to [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Miss Okonjo]].
CM: This is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Adaeze Okonjo]], hi. Who am I speaking with?
MEMBER: It's [[NAME:Hector]], [[NAME:Hector Ruiz]]. My English is not so good, sorry, I'm better in [[LANGUAGE:Spanish]].
CM: That's okay, [[NAME:Mister Ruiz]], I can get an interpreter if you want, or we can try in English first.
MEMBER: English is okay. Slow. I have bedbugs. In the bed, in the couch, everywhere. Three weeks now.
CM: Oh no. Are you getting bites?
MEMBER: Yes, my arms, my back. Very bad. I scratch at night, and with my sugar, the diabetes, I am afraid of infection.
CM: You're right to worry about that. Any redness spreading, warm, pus?
MEMBER: One on the leg is red. Big.
CM: Okay, I want you to have that looked at. I'll call [[FACILITY_NAME:Brockton Neighborhood Health]] to see if they can see you [[DATE:tomorrow]]. Have you told the building?
MEMBER: I tell the office two times... no... I tell them [[DATE:September fifteen]] and again [[DATE:last week]]. They say they will spray. Nobody comes.
CM: Okay. Let's file a complaint with the [[ORGANIZATION:Brockton Housing Authority]]. You're still at [[ADDRESS:eight hundred Pruitt Avenue]]?
MEMBER: Yes, apartment, um, [[ADDRESS:eleven C]]. [[ADDRESS:Eleven, C like cat]].
CM: [[ADDRESS:Eleven C]]. And a phone number they can call?
MEMBER: [[PHONE:Five oh eight, five five five, zero one one seven]]. Or my daughter, [[RELATIVE_NAME:Marisol]], she speaks English good.
CM: What's her number?
MEMBER: [[PHONE:Five oh eight, five five five, zero one... six six]].
CM: Okay. I'm filing it online right now. They gave me a complaint number, [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:H C, two six, zero four, four one]]. I'll text it to you.
MEMBER: Thank you. And for the bites, can I use Benadryl?
CM: The cream or a tablet at night is usually okay, but let the doctor look at the leg first. I'll call you back with the appointment.

scenario: Home health scheduler sets up wound-care nurse start of care with member's daughter
text:
SCHEDULER: Hi, this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Lorena]] calling from [[ORGANIZATION:Amberfield Home Health]]. I'm trying to reach the family of [[NAME:Opal Abernathy]]?
DAUGHTER: This is her daughter, [[RELATIVE_NAME:Celeste]]. Is this about the wound nurse?
SCHEDULER: Yes! We got the referral from Cadence and from [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Whitaker]]'s office. It looks like she has a stage three pressure injury on the sacrum and she'll need a wound vac.
DAUGHTER: Yes, they put the vac on at the hospital before she left. She came home [[DATE:Saturday]].
SCHEDULER: Okay. So the wound nurse would come out three times a week, Monday, Wednesday, Friday, for dressing changes. For the start of care, our nurse [[PROVIDER_NAME:Kateryna]] can come [[DATE:Tuesday the fourteenth]], late morning?
DAUGHTER: [[DATE:Tuesday the]]... wait, isn't that too long? The hospital said someone would come within forty-eight hours.
SCHEDULER: Sorry, you're right, I'm looking at the wrong week. Let me... [[DATE:tomorrow]], [[DATE:Tuesday]], eleven o'clock.
DAUGHTER: Okay, [[DATE:tomorrow]] at eleven. I'll be there, I'm taking off work.
SCHEDULER: Great. Can I confirm the address? I have [[ADDRESS:two twenty-nine Bramble Ridge Lane]].
DAUGHTER: That's right. It's a gated community, the gate code is [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:four four one seven pound]].
SCHEDULER: [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:Four four one seven pound]]. And her date of birth?
DAUGHTER: [[DOB:The thirtieth of July, nineteen forty]].
SCHEDULER: And the Medicare or plan ID, just to verify eligibility?
DAUGHTER: I have the Cadence card, it's [[MEMBER_ID:A B, nine three, oh oh seven, five two]], hold on, the last digit might be an eight, it's smudged.
SCHEDULER: No problem, I'll verify with the plan. And your number?
DAUGHTER: [[PHONE:Eight six five, five five five, zero one two two]].
SCHEDULER: Perfect. And [[NAME:Mrs. Abernathy]] is she on any blood thinners?
DAUGHTER: Aspirin eighty-one, that's it. And she's diabetic, A1c was seven something.
SCHEDULER: Okay, thank you, [[RELATIVE_NAME:Celeste]]. [[PROVIDER_NAME:Kateryna]] will call about thirty minutes before.

scenario: Care manager reminds hard-of-hearing member about cognitive screening; husband takes over the call
text:
CM: Hi, is this [[NAME:Mrs. Fenwick]]?
MEMBER: Mrs. who?
CM: [[NAME:Fenwick]]. [[NAME:Beatrice Fenwick]]?
MEMBER: Oh, yes, yes, that's me, sorry, I don't have my hearing aids in. Who's calling?
CM: It's [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Nadia]], from Cadence, your care manager.
MEMBER: [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Lydia]]?
CM: [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Nadia]]. [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:N, like Nancy]]. That's alright. I'm calling to remind you about your memory check appointment.
MEMBER: My what? Hold on, let me give you to [[RELATIVE_NAME:Lloyd]]. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Lloyd]]! It's the insurance.
HUSBAND: Hello, this is her husband.
CM: Hi, Mister [[RELATIVE_NAME:Fenwick]], it's [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Nadia]] from Cadence. I'm calling to remind [[NAME:Bea]] about her cognitive screening appointment [[DATE:next Monday]] at [[FACILITY_NAME:Elmhurst Senior Health]].
HUSBAND: [[DATE:Monday]]. What time?
CM: Ten fifteen, with [[PROVIDER_NAME:nurse practitioner Delgado]]. It's about an hour. They'll do a short memory test, the MoCA, and some blood work, B twelve, thyroid.
HUSBAND: She's been repeating herself a lot. Asked me four times [[DATE:yesterday]] if I fed the cat. We don't have a cat anymore.
CM: That's exactly the kind of thing to bring up. It'd be great if you could come with her and share what you've noticed.
HUSBAND: I'll drive her. [[FACILITY_NAME:Elmhurst]], that's the one on [[ADDRESS:Prairie Avenue]]?
CM: Yes, [[ADDRESS:twenty-one hundred Prairie]], second floor. Park in the back lot.
HUSBAND: Okay. Do we need to bring anything?
CM: Her medication list, her hearing aids, please, and her glasses. And the card. Just to double check, I have her birthday as [[DOB:the eleventh of April]]?
HUSBAND: [[DOB:April eleventh]], yes. She'll be seventy-seven.
CM: Perfect. I'll also send a reminder text to [[PHONE:six three oh, five five five, zero one zero nine]], is that your cell?
HUSBAND: That's mine. Good, she won't look at hers.
CM: Thank you, Mister [[RELATIVE_NAME:Fenwick]]. Have a good weekend.

scenario: Device company tech walks member through fall-detection pendant activation and emergency contacts
text:
TECH: Okay, [[NAME:Miss Agnes]], this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Kyle]] again from [[ORGANIZATION:SafeStep Alert]]. Did the box come?
MEMBER: It came, it's sitting right here on the kitchen table. I'm scared to open it.
TECH: Ha, it won't bite. Go ahead and open it, you'll see a little base unit and a pendant, it looks like a big button on a cord.
MEMBER: Okay... okay, I see it. Lord, it's big.
TECH: You can wear it on the wrist strap too. So first, flip the base over. There's a serial number on a white sticker, can you read it to me?
MEMBER: Let me get my glasses. S, S... [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:S S, seven, four, oh, nine, two, two, K as in, um, kite, one]].
TECH: [[OTHER_UNIQUE_ID:S S seven four zero nine two two K one]]. Perfect, that matches your account.
MEMBER: My nephew set up the account. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Desmond]]. He did it on the computer.
TECH: Right, I see him as the first emergency contact. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Desmond Obi]], [[PHONE:three one four, five five five, zero one nine eight]]?
MEMBER: That's him. And put my neighbor, she has a key. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Ms. Pearl]]... no, she moved. Just put [[RELATIVE_NAME:Desmond]].
TECH: Okay. And the address responders would come to, I have [[ADDRESS:sixty-eight forty Delmar Boulevard, apartment two]], [[CITY:University City]].
MEMBER: Yes. Tell them to come to the side door on [[ADDRESS:Kingsland]], the front steps are broken.
TECH: Good to know. I'll add a note, side door on [[ADDRESS:Kingsland]]. Now plug the base into the wall and press the button on the pendant.
MEMBER: Okay, pressing... it's talking!
TECH: That's our monitoring center. Answer them.
MEMBER: Hello? Yes, this is a test. I'm fine. ... They said okay.
TECH: You're all set. It'll also detect a fall automatically. Wear it in the shower, it's waterproof. You fell [[DATE:in August]], right? That's what the referral said.
MEMBER: [[DATE:August the second]]. I laid on that floor four hours.
TECH: Well, that won't happen again. I'll email the account summary to [[EMAIL:agnes w o at example dot com]].
MEMBER: That's [[RELATIVE_NAME:Desmond]]'s idea, that email. He reads it for me.

scenario: Transplant coordinator and care manager review outstanding evaluation items and living donor workup
text:
TX_COORD: Hi, [[PROVIDER_NAME:Ellen Brandt]], pre-transplant coordinator at [[FACILITY_NAME:Meridian Transplant Institute]]. I'm calling about [[NAME:Samuel Adeyemi]].
CM: Hi [[PROVIDER_NAME:Ellen]], this is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Gabriel]] at Cadence. Thanks for calling back. Where are we with [[NAME:Sam]]?
TX_COORD: So he's close. Before we can present him at selection committee, I still need the dental clearance and the colonoscopy. Everything else is done, cardiac stress test was fine, his PRA is low, blood type O positive.
CM: Dental, he saw [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Haskins]] [[DATE:on the twentieth]], I think they pulled two teeth. I'll get the letter faxed.
TX_COORD: Great. And the colonoscopy?
CM: Scheduled for [[DATE:November third]] at [[FACILITY_NAME:Saint Brendan's]] endoscopy. He was worried about the prep with his dialysis, so we moved it off a dialysis day.
TX_COORD: Smart. He dialyzes Monday Wednesday Friday?
CM: Mm-hm, and his GFR is about eleven. He's been on dialysis about three years now.
TX_COORD: Okay. Also his brother called us about being a living donor.
CM: [[RELATIVE_NAME:Tunde]]?
TX_COORD: Yes, [[RELATIVE_NAME:Babatunde Adeyemi]]. He completed the online questionnaire, and we'll do his workup separately, he'll have his own coordinator for privacy reasons. I can't share his results with you.
CM: Understood. Can you give me [[NAME:Sam]]'s medical record number at [[FACILITY_NAME:Meridian]], so I can match it in our system?
TX_COORD: [[MRN:M T I, two zero zero, eight one, five five four]].
CM: [[MRN:Two zero zero, eight one, five... five four]]?
TX_COORD: [[MRN:Five five four]]. Yes.
CM: Thanks. And should the dental letter go to you directly?
TX_COORD: Email is easiest, [[EMAIL:e brandt at example dot org]], that's [[EMAIL:e, b, r, a, n, d, t]].
CM: Got it. I'll call [[NAME:Sam]] [[DATE:this afternoon]] and let him know.
TX_COORD: Tell him he's doing great. Hoping we can list him [[DATE:before Thanksgiving]].

scenario: Care manager coaches member on setting a quit date and starting nicotine replacement
text:
CM: Hi [[NAME:Darlene]], it's [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Monique]], your care manager. You said to call around now?
MEMBER: Yeah, I'm on my break. Sorry if it's loud, the fryer's going. I'm at [[EMPLOYER:Kessler's Diner]] till three.
CM: No problem. So, we talked about picking a quit date. Did you think about it?
MEMBER: I did. I want to do [[DATE:the first of November]]. My grandson [[RELATIVE_NAME:Jaylen]] turns six [[DATE:the twelfth]], and I want to be able to hug him without smelling like an ashtray.
CM: That's a great reason. How much are you smoking right now?
MEMBER: Pack and a half a day. Thirty-some years. More when I'm stressed, which is always.
CM: Okay. And [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Varga]] said with your COPD the patch plus the gum or lozenge would be a good combo. Twenty-one milligram patch to start, and then the lozenge for cravings.
MEMBER: What about the Chantix? My cousin did that.
CM: That's an option too, you can ask him at your next visit. Some people do both. Are you okay starting with the patch?
MEMBER: Yeah. I'll try the patch.
CM: Good. I'll put the order in, it'll go to your pharmacy, the one on [[ADDRESS:Wooster Road]]?
MEMBER: Yeah, that one.
CM: There's also the free quitline, one eight hundred quit now, they'll call you weekly if you want a coach.
MEMBER: Maybe. I don't like talking on the phone that much. No offense.
CM: None taken, ha. Do you want me to check in with you the week of [[DATE:the first]], then?
MEMBER: Yeah, you can text me, it's easier. [[PHONE:Two one six, five five five, zero one... sorry, zero one seven two]].
CM: [[PHONE:Two one six, five five five, zero one seven two]]. Got it. And what's your plan for the morning cigarette with coffee? That's usually the hardest one.
MEMBER: I'm gonna switch to tea. And sit on the porch instead of the car.
CM: I love that. Okay, [[NAME:Darlene]], I'm proud of you.
